slides.title: Working practice
bullets: Never pipette material by mouth — use a rubber bulb; do not use glassware or tubes with chipped edges, discard them.

Do not recap or detach the needle by hand: discard the needle and syringe as one unit at once into a puncture-resistant sharps container within arm’s reach; if recapping is unavoidable, use only the one-hand scoop technique.
Capillary blood from the finger is taken only with sterile materials and single-use scarifiers.
The workplace must be tidy, with no unnecessary objects on the desk and the disinfection containers close to the place of analysis; electrical instruments are earthed.

slides.title: Working practice
bullets: It is forbidden to keep unlabelled reagents, to taste or smell unknown substances, or to keep poisonous, highly flammable and explosive substances on work benches.

slides.title: Purpose and stages
bullets: Quality control (internal control) in clinical diagnostic laboratories is carried out every day, in every analytical series.
Pre-analytical stage: preparing the patient, collecting the material, registration, primary handling of the specimen, delivery to the laboratory and storage until the test.
Analytical stage: that the method was chosen correctly, material and reagents were dosed correctly, and the reaction, measurement and calculation were done correctly.
Final stage: that forms are filled in correctly, the results are evaluated and the conditions for reaching the treating physician.
